claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.2 - 60 frames writing x and y adds 12,000 structs across 200 shapes
why: structural: a deterministic struct count, bit-identical across runs. Any change means Item.mergeWith behaviour changed and the one-hot-key rule needs revisiting.

claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.2 - the same 60 frames writing ONE transform key adds 200
why: structural, as above. This is the 60x that justifies geometry living in one key.

claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.10 - encodeStateAsUpdateV2 is 26.8x smaller than the append-only log, losslessly
why: structural: the simulation is deterministic and reproduced identically across two runs.

claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.7 - a 50,000-rect board is a ~7.8MB V1 blob applied in ONE uninterruptible transaction
why: structural: the blob size is deterministic and the single-transaction shape of applyUpdate is what makes cold open the worst frame in the app. This REPLACES the absolute-milliseconds gate (D-7, 2026-09-05): the same code measured 1,838 / 1,939 / 488 / 748 ms across four runs on one laptop, a 4x spread that no honest tolerance covers. The timing distribution is published in docs/measurements.md with its envelope; it is a measurement, not a gate.

claim: Phase 0 spike - moving a 50,000-shape OBJECT scene across a worker boundary costs ~261ms
why: timing, hardware-bound. The claim is the order of magnitude: an object scene costs hundreds of ms to cross, which is the same order as the decode a worker is meant to hide - so the transport must be typed arrays.

claim: PHASES.md 4.C3 - a 60-frame drag as one transaction per frame is 60 update messages on the wire
why: structural: one transaction is one update, by definition of naive. Measured to make the counterfactual concrete, not to be met.

claim: PHASES.md 4.C3 - the same drag committed on pointerup is exactly ONE update message
why: structural, tolerance 0: one gesture is one transaction. A second update means a frame leaked past the pointerup boundary.

claim: PHASES.md 4.C3 - bytes on the wire, naive over pointerup, for a 60-frame single-shape drag
why: REGISTERED 2026-09-05 BEFORE MEASURING. `expected` is the prediction (~40x); the tolerance window's floor, 40 * (1 - 0.75) = 10x, is the pre-registered requirement from PHASES.md. A reading under 10x fails the phase; a reading far from 40x means the model was wrong and the write-up says so.
